lessons: Brimstone Volley taken first in pack 2 was played twice and helped my WR deck go 3-0 in matches, contradicting the guide's claim that red removal goes unused; take it when red is open.
Abbey Griffin, Chapel Geist, Rebuke and Geistflame gave WR evasion and cheap removal that broke the stalls, matching the guide's 'evasion plus removal breaks stalls' advice.
Two Elder Cathar, Thraben Sentry and Ashmouth Hound at the bottom of the curve gave early blockers; cutting black filler for a clean two-colour core went 6-1 in games.

Dead Weight and Victim of Night carried this UB deck, but I went only 3-5 in games, so prioritise cheap early creatures and blockers over top-end, since my 2-0 loss to two Brimstone Volley and two Elder Cathar deck showed early pressure punishes slow starts.

Curse of Oblivion, Curse of the Bloody Tome, Graveyard Shovel and Inquisitor's Flail were picks I never played, so once removal and two colours are set, take playable creatures over Curses and equipment.
Plan for a long grind: my Round 3 game 2 went to 29 turns, so take Stitched Drake- or Moon Heron-style evasive threats and keep a reliable finisher to close stalled games.

Late in pack 2 I took Naturalize and Memory's Journey over playable green creatures, and neither made my deck, which matches the guide's warning about picks 10-14 and its advice not to main Naturalize.
My WG ran 9 Forest and 8 Plains and went 2-1, while the guide's 3-0 WG deck ran 10 and 7, so count pips for the heavier colour before copying a split.
My WG had only three evasive threats (two Voiceless Spirit and Spectral Rider) and lost 1-2 to WR in 13- to 22-turn games, so take a third flier over ground filler in pack 3.
Don't splash green on six Forests: my RG deck went 3-5 in games while leaning on Ambush Viper, Darkthicket Wolf, Festerhide Boar and Hamlet Captain; play two colours or run seven-plus Forests.
Prioritise answers to fliers: my ground-bound RG deck lost to Voiceless Spirit in Round 1 and Stitched Drake and Moon Heron in Round 2, with only Geistflame and Harvest Pyre as answers.
Commit to colours before pack 3: I first-picked Murder of Crows there, a blue card that went unplayed in my red-green deck, wasting a top pick.

Tonight's WB deck had no evasive fliers and lost 0-2 to BG's Somberwald Spiders in a 40-turn grind, so the guide's rule of four flier answers plus evasive finishers matters: take Chapel Geist or Voiceless Spirit over Cloistered Youth.

Round 2's 27-turn and Round 3's 40-turn losses show that a WB deck with Curse of Death's Hold and two Silverchase Fox still stalls out, so keep a real late finisher and avoid one-for-one ground filler.
Prioritise cheap interaction: my UB deck went 4-4 in games, and its only answers to RG's Riot Devils and Pitchburn Devils were Claustrophobia, Grasp of Phantoms and Sensory Deprivation.
The evasion plan won: Invisible Stalker x2 and Screeching Bat carried the 24- and 31-turn wins over BG, but the 35-turn RG loss shows it needs faster starts.
Don't overvalue card selection: my deck ran Think Twice, Forbidden Alchemy and Curiosity, yet lost 1-2 to WB and RG in games of 16 to 35 turns, so prioritise a faster curve.
Tonight's UB decks beat my BG deck 2-1 and 0-2, contradicting the guide's 44% UB rating, so don't write off UB as a weak colour.
Take a second Victim of Night as well as a second Dead Weight; my BG deck ran one of each through 25- to 39-turn losses to UB.
My BG build broke the guide's rule against double pips in both colours: Victim of Night and Screeching Bat are BB, Somberwald Spider is GG, on only 7 black sources.
Blue-black was the deepest pair; Claustrophobia, Sensory Deprivation and two Makeshift Mauler won both 2-1 matches, so take removal and efficient creatures in that colour early.
Against the red-white deck (Brimstone Volley x2, Geistflame), fragile creatures like Typhoid Rats and Brain Weevil were exposed to burn; value sturdier bodies and answers to its fliers.
Delver, Dissipate and pick-one Lost in the Mist went unused; the 17-land blue-black deck needed bodies and removal, so take those over counterspells and tricks.
